newsitem.title: USA: Banyan says sees Q4 loss, charge, new CEO.
newsitem.headline: Banyan says sees Q4 loss, charge, new CEO.

text.p: Banyan Systems Inc said Thursday that it expects to record a loss in the fourth quarter of 1996, as well as lower revenues, related to its plan to "substantially reduce" its worldwide channel inventories.

The company also said in a release Thursday that it began a search for a new chief executive officer as well as a corporate restructuring program which it expects will result in a charge of $3 to $5 million for the fourth quarter of 1996.
Chief Executive Officer David Mahoney, who founded the company in 1983, will become vice chairman of the board of directors, Banyan said.

Banyan said that the restructuring charge will provide for severance costs related to the elimination of about 100 positions, or 15 percent of its worldwide workforce, facility consolidations and other related costs.
The company said it was going forward with an executive management realignment and corporate restructuring to improve the development and delivery of its core directory and messaging solutions.

It added that the plan to reduce inventories will include a decrease in product shipments to its channel by about $7 to $10 million, thus resulting in lower revenues and a loss for the fourth quarter of 1996.
Banyan also said it expects to take a non-cash charge for previously recorded deferred tax assets in the fourth quarter of this year.
